correctness.rationale: For independent driftless Brownian particles with diffusion D>0 reset together at the first +L hit, the reflection kernel gives excursion survival erf(L/sqrt(4Ds))²~(L²/(πD))/s, an infinite-mean renewal law. Erickson's cited index-one renewal theorem supplies the logarithmic age U~Unif[0,1]; conditioning on the last renewal yields independent killed-Brownian coordinates with exact density q_epsilon(y)=(exp(-(y-epsilon)²)-exp(-(y+epsilon)²))/(sqrt(pi) erf(epsilon)), which converges in total variation to 2yexp(-y²). Together they yield joint age–Rayleigh independence, both log-distance exponents U/2, and ratio density 2r/(1+r²)². Positive age moments E[A_t^v]~t^v/(v log(t/t0)) for fixed v>0 via index-one strong renewal yield the claimed joint moments and Pearson π/4; centering is lower order. Independently checked conditioned density normalization numerically at eps=0.5,0.1,0.02 and the Gamma coefficient identity. Finite quadrature is not an asymptotic proof; renewal theorem assumptions include smooth nonarithmetic first-hit distribution.

originality.rationale: Biroli–Majumdar–Schehr's First Passage Resetting Gas establishes the model and N=2 absence of stationary density but not the critical joint nonstationary age/position/Rayleigh-ratio/moment limit. Erickson 1970 already proves the logarithmic renewal age; it is explicitly credited and excluded from novelty. De Mauro et al finite-mean sampled resetting intervals have a different renewal protocol. The new statement is the combined conditional spatial and exact moment/ratio consequences at the specifically first-hit-coupled N=2 threshold.
